1 What Trump actually changed in military law

Signed March 1, 2018, by Trump, 
it implemented substantial military justice reforms, including provisions of the Military Justice Act of 2016, with major changes effective January 1, 2019

The order addressed:
1 Rules for Courts-Martial, including charging, trials, and sentencing
2 Military Rules of Evidence.
3 Punitive articles defining military offenses.

5 Implementation of reforms previously enacted by Congress

Yes, within the applicable jurisdiction of military law.
The UCMJ addresses serious offenses that may include
UCMJ provisions:

Article 94 - Mutiny and sedition
Article 103 - Spies
Article 103a - Espionage
Article 104 - Aiding the enemy
Article 107 - False official statements
Article 131 - Perjury
Article 132 - Retaliation

🎙 Iran, China hold investment forum to explore new cooperation opportunities

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Iran and China have held an investment and trade forum in Shanghai to explore new opportunities for cooperation and expand bilateral trade and investment ties, bringing together economic and diplomatic officials, major Iranian companies and Chinese business representatives.

The event was held on the sidelines of the ninth China International Import Expo (CIIE) on Sunday, with around 300 participants, including business representatives, trade associations, chambers of commerce and Chinese official institutions.
​
Participants discussed Iran’s investment, export and industrial capabilities across various sectors.
​
Iranian Ambassador to China Abdolreza Rahmani Fazli, addressing the forum, highlighted the 55th anniversary of the establishment of modern diplomatic relations between the two countries and the 10th anniversary of their comprehensive strategic partnership.
​
He stressed the need to capitalize on existing capacities to expand economic and technological cooperation.
​
Rahmani Fazli said Iranian companies were showcasing their capabilities in energy, petrochemicals, mining, agriculture, food industries and emerging technologies at the expo.
​
He added that Iran’s national pavilion was also highlighting the country’s scientific and technological achievements, including medical diagnostic equipment, nanomedicine, biopharmaceuticals and medicinal plants, which could provide opportunities for developing joint value chains with Chinese companies.
​
The ambassador identified joint research, emerging industries, clean production, technical standards, infrastructure, renewable energy, smart transportation and the green economy as other promising areas for cooperation.
​
He expressed hope that the forum would facilitate direct contacts between businesses, investors and companies from both countries, helping identify joint projects and turn the opportunities presented into practical cooperation.

🧠 Your trade nears its profit target, then turns and hits the stop. Holding for a planned target is reasonable. Believing the market must reach it is not: no outcome is guaranteed.

That belief can point to a need for certainty. You may accept losses, yet hesitate to close a winning trade in case it climbs further. Fear of missing out can push you to break your own rules.

Tino’s time-stop exercise helps examine this reaction. For a series of trades, set a fixed holding period and exit when the timer ends. Keep your risk limits in place. The exercise is about behaviour, not profit.

Track how you feel at the timed exit and whether you delay. Did the possibility of further gains make you ignore your commitment? If the target is reached later, that does not mean you could have known it would happen.
